title: Continuous Cech cocycles with finite ell-adic field coefficients are coboundaries
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extending nonarchimedean norm topology. Put $F=E$; in particular, $F$ is complete. Work in the profinite universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; a profinite set means a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space. Let $q:T\to S$ be any continuous surjection of profinite sets. For $n\geq0$ put $T_S^{n+1}=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in T^{n+1}:q(t_0)=\cdots=q(t_n)\}$ with the subspace topology. Let $C_n=C(T_S^{n+1},F)$, where $C(-,F)$ consists of all continuous functions, with pointwise addition [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Define $d_n:C_n\to C_{n+1}$ by
$$ (d_nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j f(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1}). $$
Then for every integer $n\geq1$ and every $f\in C_n$ with $d_nf=0$, there exists $g\in C_{n-1}$ with $d_{n-1}g=f$. The empty surjection is included. The assertion is about these actual continuous-function groups with values in the fixed complete field E, without replacement by locally constant functions.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2)–(4) and its proof, with G=1: discrete coefficients, sequential profinitely split inverse limits, and sequential closed colimits. Agent-formulated Cech consequence for finite E, obtained from O_E = lim O_E/pi^m and E = colim pi^(-m) O_E; not asserted for the noncomplete norm-topological algebraic closure. Blueprint motivation: main-20261015 direct-images proof paragraph (3), finite E branch.

proof.text: Put $P_r=T_S^r$. Repeatedly apply [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] to $P_{r+1}=P_r\times_S T$, starting with $P_1=T$. It gives the compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topology on every $P_r$; the tuple identification and its inverse are the coordinate maps. Deleting a coordinate is continuous. Thus every displayed differential is continuous. In $d_{k+1}d_k$, deleting positions $i<j$ in the two possible orders gives the same function with opposite signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, so $d_{k+1}d_k=0$. If $T=S=\varnothing$, every cochain group is zero and $g=0$ proves the claim. We may henceforth work with nonempty $S$ (surjectivity makes $T$ nonempty).

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2)–(4), explicit Cech expansion: domains and differentials. Profinite fibre products are the Stacks 08ZY/0A2P input recorded by the cited node.

proof.text:
First let $M$ be any finite discrete abelian group and let $c\in C(P_{n+1},M)$ be a cocycle, with $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-valued-cech-cocycle-descent] to obtain $q_0:T_0\twoheadrightarrow S_0$, $a,b$ and $c_0$ with $d_nc_0=0$. Choose a set section $\sigma:S_0\to T_0$; it is continuous since both sets are finite discrete. Put
$$v_0(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=c_0(\sigma(q_0(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}).$$
For an equal-image tuple $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, the equation $d_nc_0=0$ on $(\sigma(q_0(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ reads
$$c_0(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j c_0(\sigma(q_0(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_n).$$
All base images are equal, so the sum is $d_{n-1}v_0$. Precompose $v_0$ with $a$ in every coordinate. The resulting continuous $v:P_n\to M$ satisfies $d_{n-1}v=c$, since coordinate deletion commutes with $a$. This proves the finite-coefficient assertion used below, including $n=1$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2), discrete coefficients: agent expansion through finite quotient descent and the explicit extra-coordinate contraction.

proof.text:
Use the coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and put $O=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] choose a nonzero uniformizer $\pi$ with $0<|\pi|_E<1$ and $\pi O=\mathfrak m_E$; $O$ is a DVR with finite residue field. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A_m=O/\pi^mO$ is finite for every $m\geq1$ and $p_m:A_{m+1}\to A_m$ is surjective. By [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower], the reduction map
$$O\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{m\geq1}A_m$$
is a topological ring isomorphism for the discrete quotient topologies. In particular each reduction $O\to A_m$ is continuous and the reductions jointly distinguish elements of $O$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), the sequential limit of discrete integral quotients: local field data and the topological inverse-limit input are supplied by the cited arithmetic nodes.

proof.text:
Temporarily suppose $f:P_{n+1}\to O$ is a continuous cocycle. Write $f_m$ for its reduction in $A_m$; then $d_nf_m=0$ because reduction is additive. Step 2 with $M=(A_1,+)$ gives a continuous $g_1:P_n\to A_1$ with $d_{n-1}g_1=f_1$. We construct by induction continuous $g_m:P_n\to A_m$ with
$$d_{n-1}g_m=f_m,\qquad p_mg_{m+1}=g_m.$$
The first equation at $m=1$ is the base case just obtained. The next two steps give the induction step for every $m\geq1$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), agent expansion: initialize a compatible sequence of integral primitives, rather than choosing unrelated primitives at every level.

proof.text:
Assume $g_m$ is constructed. Choose a set section $s_m:A_m\to A_{m+1}$ of the surjection $p_m$ from [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]; it is continuous between finite discrete spaces. Thus $\widetilde g=s_m\circ g_m$ is a continuous lift; no additivity of $s_m$ is assumed. Set
$$r=d_{n-1}\widetilde g-f_{m+1}.$$
The additive map $p_m$ sends $r$ to $d_{n-1}g_m-f_m=0$. Hence $r$ is a continuous cochain with values in the finite discrete abelian group $K_m=\ker(p_m)$: it is continuous as a map to the subset $K_m\subseteq A_{m+1}$. Further,
$$d_nr=d_nd_{n-1}\widetilde g-d_nf_{m+1}=0$$
by step 1 and the cocycle equation for $f$. The same equation holds in $K_m$ because its inclusion is injective.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), explicit profinitely split coefficient transition and its finite-kernel obstruction cocycle.

proof.text:
Apply the finite-coefficient result of step 2 to $M=K_m$ and this degree-$n$ cocycle $r$. It gives continuous $v:P_n\to K_m$ with $d_{n-1}v=r$. Let $\iota_m:K_m\hookrightarrow A_{m+1}$ be the inclusion and define
$$g_{m+1}=\widetilde g-\iota_m v.$$
Then $p_mg_{m+1}=g_m$, since $p_m\iota_m=0$, and
$$d_{n-1}g_{m+1}=d_{n-1}\widetilde g-\iota_mr=f_{m+1}.$$
This completes the stated induction. It works in degree $n=1$: it solves a $K_m$-valued degree-one cocycle by a degree-zero cochain, and uses no negative degree or degree-zero vanishing claim.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), explicit finite-kernel correction producing compatible primitives.

proof.text: For each $x\in P_n$, the compatible tuple $(g_m(x))_{m\geq1}$ lies in $\varprojlim_mA_m$. The map to the product is continuous because each coordinate $g_m$ is continuous; corestricting to the compatibility subspace preserves continuity. Compose with the inverse homeomorphism in [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] to obtain a continuous $g_O:P_n\to O$. For every $m$, the reduction of $d_{n-1}g_O$ is $d_{n-1}g_m=f_m$, since the reduction maps preserve finite signed sums. The ring-isomorphism part of that node makes the reductions jointly injective, so $d_{n-1}g_O=f$ as actual $O$-valued functions. This proves the integral assertion without any exchange of cohomology and inverse limits.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), explicit inverse-limit reconstruction and equality checked in every finite quotient.

proof.text:
Return to the given $E$-valued cocycle $f$. The open sets
$$U_k=\{x\in P_{n+1}:|f(x)|_E<|\pi|_E^{-k}\}\qquad(k\geq0)$$
cover $P_{n+1}$ because $0<|\pi|_E<1$. Compactness of $P_{n+1}$ from [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] gives a finite subcover. The $U_k$ are increasing; take its largest index $k$. Then $|\pi^kf(x)|_E<1$ for every $x$, so $h=\pi^kf$ is a continuous $O$-valued cocycle, with $O$ carrying its subspace topology. The integral result of steps 4–7 gives continuous $u:P_n\to O$ with $d_{n-1}u=h$. Set $g=\pi^{-k}u:P_n\to E$. Multiplication by this fixed field element is continuous, and linearity of the finite signed sum gives
$$d_{n-1}g=\pi^{-k}d_{n-1}u=\pi^{-k}\pi^kf=f.$$
No local constancy is imposed on $f,u$ or $g$.
